title: conversion of all values to zero during the matrix multiplication with a scalar in the implementation of a neural network in C
body_html:

I am getting all the values to zero. When this happens, the weights are not updated. I am new to this programming language just coupe of months of reading this language. I want to understand why I am getting this error. You can look at code line no 369 and 372.

I was expecting the values to change in every time in each iteration such at certain time I would get the best possible result.

events.body_html: Side note: Things like (*matrix).rows are commonly written in the equivalent form: matrix->rows
Note that in matrixformation you probably want to verify that malloc succeeded. In the loop, if malloc fails, you'll want to free previously allocated rows to avoid a memory leak.
Note that for functions add() and subtract(), compiler reports "warning: control reaches end of non-void function" for the partial handling of the failure cases.

My comments where more general, not focused directly on your issue. The first was a style issue that affects readers, but has no impact on operation of the code. The second was about 2 errors in the code that the compiler detects & warns about. These need to be fixed, but are not necessarily related to the problem you are experiencing. They do highlight that your error handling has holes.

I looked at your scalarm() and the only issues I found were that it does not handle potential failure of matrixformation() and that matrixformation() does not handle potential malloc() failures. Other than that, if an issue is occurring there, it could be a symptom of a problem that actually occurred earlier. Purely as a guess, I'd suspect some failure or bug related to memory handling. I'd suggest tightening up your error handling, working up a minimal reproducible example, and using a debugger.

Regarding the malloc failures, unless you plan on some sort of graceful handling (e.g. in an interpreted environment that is probably needed) just log an error and abort and let the OS take care of cleaning up the memory. Or if you want to be lazy don't even do that, let the resulting segmentation fault happen, and let the OS provide the user with a message about it crashing (though it won't necessarily convey that it was because it ran out of memory).
